title: Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer
tagline: Every choice you make builds your future self.
credits: Story state machine for the web player. Code and text written with AI assistance (Claude Fable 5.2); idea and direction by Faris.

weather.name: Space-weather scientist
weather.does: Reads the Sun and buys warning time

doctor.name: Space doctor
doctor.does: Keeps the crew in one piece

farmer.name: Space farmer
farmer.does: Grows the food and the air

fact.text: Real: in April 2026 a Saudi satellite called SHAMS flew toward the Moon with the Artemis II crew, to measure radiation from the Sun.
Real: the Madak space competition (2024) was open to ages 6 to 18. Ten winning experiments flew to the International Space Station.
Real: two Saudi astronauts flew to the International Space Station in May 2023, and the SARI 2 programme helps university students build and launch small satellites.

choice.prompt: The storm is coming. Use the warning time.

options.label: Bury the shelter
options.why: Moon dirt on the roof blocks radiation. The rover drains the batteries.

options.label: Charge up
options.why: Full batteries for the long wait. The roof stays thin.

options.label: Call it early
options.why: You read the first particles and start sooner. Time for both jobs, but nobody checks the air system.

fact.text: Real: in the September 2017 storm, a detector inside the Space Station read about 1.5 times its normal dose. A thinly shielded detector in lunar orbit read more than 1,000 times. Shielding matters.

choice.prompt: Batteries are dropping. The greenhouse lights are hungry!

options.label: Lights on
options.why: The plants keep making oxygen. The lights eat power.

options.label: Lights off
options.why: Power saved. The plants stop making oxygen, and lettuce takes 3 to 4 weeks to grow back.

options.label: Use the night battery
options.why: Lights and air both run. The long lunar night will be colder.

options.label: Carry the trays in
options.why: The plants clean the air where you breathe. One last trip through the thin-walled room.

fact.text: Real: a radio message crosses from the Moon to Earth in 1.3 seconds. From Mars it can take up to 22 minutes each way, so crews must be ready to decide alone.

choice.prompt: The air cleaner froze. The reset switch is outside the shelter.

options.label: Stay put
options.why: Safe behind the thick wall. The air gets stale.

options.label: Dash out
options.why: Fresh air. You take radiation at the worst moment of the storm.

options.label: Lowest badge goes
options.why: You send whoever has taken the least radiation, for the shortest time.

options.label: Reset it by remote
options.why: You drive the rover from inside. Nobody takes a dose. The rover drains the batteries.

storms._note: One real storm is drawn at random each run. Archived NASA DONKI data: never shown as live.

jan.name: the January 2026 radiation storm
jan.facts: An X1.9 solar flare on 18 January 2026. Protons crossed the alert level about 5 hours later and climbed to 36,976 particle flux units. The eruption reached Earth about 25 hours after it left the Sun and caused a severe geomagnetic storm (Kp 8.67).

may.name: the May 2024 storm
may.facts: An X5.8 solar flare on 11 May 2024, during a Kp 9 geomagnetic storm (the top of the scale). Energetic protons arrived within about an hour.
may.taxNote: Only one hour of warning: the storm takes 1 SHIELD before you finish.
may.waivedNote: You called it early: no shield lost.

thrive.title: The outpost rode out the storm.
thrive.line: Nothing ran empty. Back to work.

lesson.title: Everyone is safe. One thing ran low.
lesson.line: Now you know why that meter matters.

evac.title: Home early, and safe.
evac.line: One meter hit empty, so the crew flew home. The next crew will use your notes.

common: Space competitions for school students, like Madak (2024), whose winning experiments flew to the Space Station.
SARI 2: build and launch a small satellite as a student team.
Saudi astronauts have already flown: two went to the Space Station in May 2023.

weather.real: SHAMS, a Saudi satellite, flew with the Artemis II crew in 2026 to measure radiation from the Sun.

power.real: A night on most of the Moon lasts about two weeks, and the surface drops below minus 170 degrees Celsius. Power is everything.

doctor.real: On long missions astronauts lose about 1 to 1.5 percent of their bone density each month. Space doctors fight that.

farmer.real: NASA grew tomatoes on the Space Station for 101 days. Lettuce takes 21 to 28 days.

comms.real: A signal from the Moon reaches Earth in 1.3 seconds. From Mars it can take 22 minutes.
